semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ}: «إذا» is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb) is «تُحَدِّثُ», which is what makes it accusative according to the majority. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that its governor be «يَصْدُرُ». Others make its governor what comes after it and immediately follows it, even though that is governed by it through annexation in the implied structure; Makkī chose this, and he made it parallel to «مَنْ» and «ما», meaning that these two govern what follows them in the jussive, while what follows them governs them in the accusative; had he illustrated it with «أيّ», it would have been clearer. It was also said: its governor is implied, i.e. "they will be gathered". It was also said: "remember"; and in that case it leaves [the function of] adverb and condition.
His saying: {زِلْزَالَهَا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its fāʿil (agent). The meaning is: its quaking that it deserves and that its mass and magnitude require. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Similar to it is: "أكرِمِ التقيَّ إكرامَه، وأَهِنِ الفاسِقَ إهانتَه" (honour the God-fearing with the honour due to him, and humiliate the sinner with the humiliation due to him); or [it means] its quaking in full.» The majority read it with kasra on the zāy.
Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā [read it] with fatḥa. It was said: they are two maṣdars with one meaning. It was also said: the kasra form is a maṣdar and the fatḥa form is a noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Among the patterns there is no فَعْلال with fatḥa except in reduplicated [roots].» I say: some have made the fatḥa form in the sense of an active participle, like صَلْصَال in the sense of مُصَلْصِل, and that has been discussed already. His saying: «Among the patterns there is no فَعْلال» means: as a rule; otherwise «ناقةٌ خَزْعال» (a limping she-camel) has occurred.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {مَا لَهَا}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). This refutes the saying of whoever said that the ḥāl (circumstantial) in such as {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49] is obligatory lest the speech become uninformative, for there is no ḥāl here.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}, i.e. on the day when it is shaken. The governor of «يومئذٍ» is «تُحَدِّثُ» if you make «إذا» accusative by what follows it or by something omitted; and if you make its governor «تُحَدِّثُ», «يومئذٍ» is a badal (substitute) from it, and its governor is [either] the governor of [«إذا»], or something else because it [the badal] is on the intention of repeating the governor — a well-known disagreement.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تُحَدِّثُ», i.e. it narrates. It may also be attached to «أخبارَها» itself. It was also said: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and «أنَّ» with what is in its domain is a badal (substitute) from «أخبارَها». It was also said: the bāʾ is causal, i.e. because of Allah the Exalted's revealing to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: where are the two objects of "تُحَدِّثُ"? I say: the first of them is omitted, and the second is "أخبارَها"; its origin is: it narrates to creation its news; except that what is intended is to mention its narrating the news, not to mention creation, in order to magnify the Day. If you say: to what is the bāʾ attached in His saying "بأنَّ ربَّك"? I say: to "تُحَدِّثُ", because its meaning is: it narrates its news because of your Lord's revealing. The meaning may also be: it narrates your Lord [sic] by narrating that your Lord revealed to it its news, on the basis that its narrating that your Lord revealed to it is a narrating of its news, just as you say: "you gave me every advice by advising me in religion".» [Translator's note: «تُحَدِّثُ ربَّك» is as written; the sense requires something like "it narrates by narrating that your Lord revealed…", and «ربَّك» here may be a copying error.] The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «It is speech containing rubbish from which the Qurʾān is to be kept free.» I say: what rubbish is there in it, given its correctness and eloquence? But since its implied structure was long on account of conveying this fine meaning, he made it rubbish — far be it from that!
Then al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is possible that "بأنَّ ربَّك" is a badal from "أخبارَها", as though it were said: on that Day it will narrate its news, that your Lord revealed to it; because you say: حَدَّثْتُه كذا and حَدَّثْتُه بكذا (I told him such-and-such / of such-and-such).» The Shaykh said: «If the verb is sometimes made transitive by a preposition and sometimes transitive by itself, and the preposition is not redundant, then in its follower only agreement in case is permissible. So "استغفَرْتُ الذنبَ العظيمِ" with "الذنبَ" in the accusative and "العظيم" in the genitive is not permissible on the grounds that you may say "من الذنب"; nor "اخْتَرْتُ زيداً الرجالَ الكرامِ" with "الرجالَ" in the accusative and "الكرام" in the genitive; likewise you may not say "استغفرتُ من الذنبِ العظيمَ" with "العظيمَ" in the accusative, and likewise with "اخْتَرْتُ". If the preposition were redundant, following the position of the noun would be permissible, under its conditions as set out in the science of grammar; you say: "ما رأيتُ مِنْ رجلٍ عاقلاً", because "مِنْ" is redundant, and "مِنْ رجل عاقلٍ" following the wording; but it is not permissible to put "رجل" in the accusative and "عاقل" in the genitive on the grounds that the entry of "مِنْ" may be taken into account. If anything of that kind occurs, its domain is poetry.» End of quotation. I do not know how he makes al-Zamakhsharī liable for what he made him liable for, from all the questions he mentioned. For al-Zamakhsharī says: this is a badal from what precedes it; then he mentioned what justifies the entry of the bāʾ on the badal, namely that the bāʾ may enter on the substituted-for word, so that were the badal to take the place of the substituted-for word with the bāʾ, it would be permissible, because the governor is made transitive by it; and he mentioned what justifies the substituted-for word's being free of the bāʾ, saying: «because you say: حَدَّثْتُه كذا and حَدَّثْتُه بكذا». As for its being prohibited to say «استغفَرتُ الذنبَ العظيمِ» with «الذنبَ» in the accusative and «العظيمِ» in the genitive, to the end — there is nothing of that at all in al-Zamakhsharī's words.
The parallel of what al-Zamakhsharī said in the case of «استغفر» is that you say: «استغفرْتُ اللَّهَ ذنباً مِنْ شَتْمي زيداً» (I asked Allah's forgiveness for a sin — for my reviling Zayd); your saying «مِنْ شَتْمي» is a badal from «الذنب», and this is permissible without doubt.
His saying: {أوحى لَهَا}: There are several views on this lām. The first: it is in the sense of «إلى»; it was preferred to «إلى» only to accord with the verse-endings (fawāṣil). Al-ʿAjjāj said, describing the earth:
4614 - أَوْحَى لها القرارَ فاستقرَّتِ ... وشَدَّها بالرَّاسياتِ الثُّبَّتِ
(He inspired it to be still, so it became still, and fastened it with the firm-set mountains.)
The second: it keeps its basic sense, and «أوحى» is made transitive sometimes with the lām and sometimes with «إلى»; from it is the preceding verse. The third: the lām has its proper sense of cause, and the one to whom revelation is made is omitted, namely the angels; its implied form is: He revealed to the angels for the sake of the earth, i.e. for the sake of what they will do in it.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: either a badal (substitute) from the «يومئذٍ» before it, or accusative by «يَصْدُرُ», or accusative by an implied «اذْكُرْ» (remember).
His saying: {أَشْتَاتاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الناس»; it is the plural of شَتّ, i.e. dispersed [in groups] in safety and fear, in whiteness and blackness.
His saying: {لِّيُرَوْاْ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَصْدُرُ»; it was also said: to «أوحى», with what is between them parenthetical. The majority read it as passive; it is from seeing with the eye, so it is made transitive by the hamza to a second [object], namely «أعمالَهم». Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Qatāda and Ḥammāda [sic] ibn Salama — and it is related from Nāfiʿ; al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is the reading of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ» — read it as active; and the meaning is: [to see] the recompense of their deeds. [Translator's note: the name is written «حمادة»; the well-known reader is Ḥammād ibn Salama.]

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {خَيْراً}, {شَرّاً}: There are two views on their accusative. The more apparent of the two: they are a tamyīz (specification) of «مثقال», since it is a measure. The second: they are two badals (substitutes) from «مثقالَ».
His saying: {يَرَهُ}: the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition in both places. Hishām read the hāʾ of «يَرَهْ» with sukūn in continuous recitation in both words, and the rest of the Seven with ḍamma, joined to a wāw in continuous recitation and quiescent in pause, like all the pronominal hāʾs. This is what I read with. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted from Hishām and Abū Bakr its sukūn, from Abū ʿAmr its ḍamma with full lengthening, and from the rest of the Seven full lengthening in the first and sukūn in the second. End of quotation. That was mostly due to the pause at the end of the sūra; had they joined its end to the beginning of «al-ʿĀdiyāt», the rule would be full lengthening. This is what their principles require, as I stated earlier, and it is what is transmitted.
The majority read «يَرَهُ» as active. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥaywa, and ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī in one transmission read «يُرَه» as passive. ʿIkrima [read] «يَراه» with the alif: either on the supposition of the jussive by omission of the implied vowel, or on the illusion that «مَنْ» is relative; the verification of this is mentioned near the end of [Sūrat] Yūsuf. Al-Zamakhsharī related that a Bedouin put «خيراً يَرَهُ» later [i.e. read the two verses in reverse order]; it was said to him: "You have put first and put last [what should not be]", and he recited:
4615 - خذا بَطْنَ هرشى أوقَفاها فإنَّه ... كِلا جانِبَيْ هرشى لَهُنَّ طريقُ
(Take the inner side of Harshā or its back, for both sides of Harshā are a road for them.)
End of quotation. He means that putting first and last are the same. This is not permissible at all, for it is an error that is not to be held as a reading.
الذَّرَّة — it was said: the small ant; and the smallest it is when a year has passed over it. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4616 - من القاصراتِ الطَرْفِ لو دَبَّ مُحْوِلٌ ... من الذَّرِّ فوق الإِتْبِ منها لأَثَّرا
(Of those who restrain their glances: were a year-old ant to creep over her shift, it would leave a mark.)
